summary: A roughly 63-minute manager 1-1 between Chris Klevan and closer Harry Edmonds, opening as a call review of Harry's Rafal Sowa call earlier the same day and running into live role-play and then unstructured personal conversation. Chris had already listened to the tail of the Rafal recording and diagnosed the loss as a failure to run the open-wallet play: Harry mentioned payment plans and moved past the financial objection without pacing or isolating it. Harry had rewritten the discovery process into his own document; Chris reviewed it, said the structure was fine but that process was not the problem — 'it's just doing it' — and pushed the issue onto Harry's own discomfort with asking about money, which Harry traced to pride about his own bank balance. They then role-played the objection handle end to end, with Chris playing Rafal, and Chris corrected the open-wallet opener to lead with monthly surplus after bills rather than cash on hand. The back half of the call is largely non-work: camera-on tactics, physique and authority, past anabolic steroid use, diet, TRT, housing and Thailand.
notable: Volume and payment-mix disclosure: Harry states 'I've noticed I've only closed like three PIFs out of 15 deals this month. It's bad because I'd be on like nearly 100k if I just open walleted them and if they had the money.' Fifteen deals in May from this rep, with only three paid in full — the corpus and the close-rate denominator should be reconciled against that number.

Stated policy on payment plans: they are treated as a fallback to be avoided, not an offer. The instruction is to run the open wallet FIRST and only structure a plan once finances are known — 'when they ask for payment plans, I need to open wallet them.' A 'six pay' instalment structure is referenced as the standard fallback pitch.

Explicit management directive that no prospect should be allowed to end a call undecided: 'When I listen to the next calls that you have today, it needs to be a clear yes or no... don't let people hop off the call.' Letting a prospect say they will think about it is characterised as the rep being selfish.

Chris coaches Harry to assume every prospect has credit cards and treat that as favourable, and recounts personally helping a previous client obtain a 0% Amex card so she could fund a $6,000 purchase two days later.

The lost prospect Rafal Sowa is discussed clinically only in passing — a surgeon with hip joint damage who does not believe he can get out of pain, taking a six-month sabbatical for mental and physical health. Chris's response to the sabbatical is 'But that's more reason for him to do the program.' Suitability of loaded kettlebell training for hip joint damage is never raised by either party.

Chris on the spouse objection in this offer: 'the partner has nothing to do with this, they're not doing the fitness... it's just always gonna come down to purely finances' — i.e. treat OB as a disguised money objection. He also notes setters usually establish whether a partner exists.

Chris on hiring and the team: 'I don't keep terrible talent around anymore', and he floats Harry as a future team leader. Kyla (setter, referenced elsewhere as setter code KL) is assessed as a future closer; Chris notes she over-uses verbal acknowledgements on Zoom.

Harry describes a deliberate opening tactic of joining calls with his camera off for a few seconds so the prospect sees his shirtless profile picture, then turning it on; he credits it with a 50% close rate and Chris tells him to bring it back.

Roughly the last 25 minutes is off-topic: Chris's competitive bodybuilding history and trenbolone use, Harry considering testosterone or RAD-140/MK-677, side effects, diet, eczema, housing and Thailand. Notable only because a manager at a fitness company is discussing personal anabolic steroid use with a rep who sells a natural fitness programme.

Diarization in this file is badly unreliable — whole passages are inverted. The bodybuilding, US-residency, wife/Dana and 5'9" material is labelled 'Harry Edmonds (Primal Instinct)' but belongs to Chris Klevan, and much of the coaching labelled 'Chris Klevan' is Harry. Note also that only one speaker carries the '(Primal Instinct)' tag, so the label heuristic alone would misclassify this as a sales call.
